Ensemble model consensus from NWS short-range guidance projects only modest daytime warming before the marine influence reasserts, consistent with climatological August patterns where coastal moderation typically limits peaks to the mid-70s to low-80s. This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pa/panama-city/MPMG.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from regional meteorological agencies indicate Panama City’s August 18 maximum will likely settle near 30–31 °C, reflecting the market’s tight clustering around those outcomes. Persistent trade-wind moisture, scattered convective clouds, and typical wet-season afternoon showers are expected to cap daytime heating, while any reduction in cloud cover or delayed rainfall could push readings to 32 °C. Historical climatology for mid-August shows a narrow interquartile range of 29.5–31.5 °C, underscoring why traders assign minimal probability outside this band. Updated model runs tonight and early-morning observations will determine whether the upper or lower edge of the 30–31 °C window prevails at resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Monsoon dynamics and short-term forecast uncertainty primarily drive the tight clustering around 32–33°C.** Active southwest monsoon conditions over northern India, including residual moisture and cloud cover from a Bay of Bengal depression, are expected to limit daytime heating in Lucknow on August 19. Recent model consensus and observational trends show daytime maxima in the low-to-mid 30s °C, with light rainfall or overcast skies further capping peaks near 32 °C (currently holding the narrowest edge in trader positioning).

Atmospheric factors differentiating the 1 °C spread include variable steering winds, localized convective activity, and exact timing of any showers, all of which can shift the daily maximum by a degree or two. Historical August baselines for Lucknow average highs near 31–32 °C under typical monsoon influence, providing context for why probabilities remain concentrated rather than skewed higher. Traders appear to weigh the latest IMD extended-range guidance and global model runs, which continue to favor modest suppression of temperatures through increased humidity and intermittent cloudiness.

Resolution hinges on the official maximum recorded on the 19th; any last-minute clearing or delayed rainfall could tip sentiment toward 33 °C, while stronger convection would reinforce the 32 °C outcome.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Manila's highest temperature on August 19 centers on 28–30°C**, with 29°C holding the highest implied probability at 37%. This distribution aligns with climatological norms and current conditions in the Philippines' southwest monsoon (habagat) season.

PAGASA forecasts for August 19 indicate a daily range of 24–31°C under continued habagat influence, with 60% chance of rain and scattered thunderstorms. Persistent cloud cover and precipitation typically cap daytime maxima near or slightly below the August average of ~30–31°C, preventing stronger heating while limiting extreme outliers above 31°C to low single-digit probabilities.

Recent model guidance and monitoring show no significant shift toward clearer skies or enhanced insolation that would push readings to 32°C or higher. Historical analogs for mid-August under active monsoon flow reinforce this range, with traders incorporating the latest PAGASA outlooks and regional observations that emphasize rain-cooled conditions over Metro Manila. The tight clustering around 28–30°C reflects this scientific consensus on monsoon-driven moderation ahead of the target date.
